headline: SHORE got its phone speedup; the fancy governor ate itself
lede: #668 shipped to prod: device-pixel-ratio capped at 2 (phones rendered 2.25x the pixels for free), offscreen render targets so the canvas never resizes, deterministic ?rs/?nsub harness locks, and a new shoreperf measurement rig. The adaptive-resolution governor and shader trims were built, measured, and backed out with evidence.

notes.text: The box runs local LLM inference and other lanes' Chrome harnesses on the same Metal GPU: absolute fps numbers there are fiction, and leaked headless Chromes from failed boots made every measurement slower than baseline. Interleaved A/B against origin/main is the only honest local signal; shorecheck and CI's dedicated box are the real gates.
nsub=2 (dt 1/120) sits on the CFL edge of the 0.4m shallow-water grid: swash depths inflated past 4m and shorecheck's trace gates broke deterministically. Sim fidelity is not a quality knob.

An adaptive 1->0.9 resolution governor starved the probe readback under contention and passed zero shorecheck runs while the locked build passed 26/26 — backed out, but the blit plumbing stays so internal resolution is lockable without ever resizing the canvas backbuffer.
shorecheck green vs red at the same minute on the same machine is a bisectable oracle: sed-disable one feature into a copy, run shorecheck --file, and the culprit falls out in two rounds.
